# Future Directions — The Möbius discriminant and log-behaviour of combinatorial totals

This cycle isolated a single scalar invariant — the **Möbius discriminant**
`Δ = γβ − αδ` attached to a first-order multiplicative recurrence
`(α n + β)·a(n+1) = (γ n + δ)·a(n)` — and proved that its sign completely
governs the log-behaviour of the sequence: strict log-convexity when `Δ > 0`,
log-linearity when `Δ = 0`, strict log-concavity when `Δ < 0`. The classical
totals `2ⁿ` (`Δ = 0`), Catalan `Cₙ` (`Δ = 6`), central binomials (`Δ = 2`),
factorials (`Δ = 1`), and reciprocal factorials (`Δ = −1`) instantiate all three
regimes, refining the earlier `d = 1` vs `d = 2` dichotomy into a genuine
sign-indexed trichotomy.

## Conjecture A — Quantitative discriminant law

For a sequence obeying the recurrence, the pointwise discriminant
`D(n) = a(n)·a(n+2) − a(n+1)²` satisfies an exact identity
`(α n + β)(α(n+1) + β)·D(n) = Δ · a(n+1)·a(n+2) · (α n + β) / (γ n + δ)` — i.e.
`D(n)` is a *fixed positive multiple of `Δ`* at every index, so its sign never
flips.

**The key insight is** that the ratio `a(n+1)/a(n)` is a Möbius transform of `n`
whose forward difference has the constant numerator `Δ`, so the "log-curvature"
of the sequence is rigidly proportional to `Δ` rather than merely sharing its
sign.

**Why now?** The ratio-as-Möbius identity established this cycle already
produces the sign law; upgrading it to an exact proportionality is the natural
strengthening and would give closed-form control of the second-order growth of
every classical combinatorial total simultaneously.

## Conjecture B — Second-order (Turán) recurrences and a discriminant polynomial

Many combinatorial totals satisfy instead a *second-order* recurrence
`p(n)·a(n+2) = q(n)·a(n+1) + r(n)·a(n)` (e.g. Motzkin, Baxter). We conjecture a
polynomial discriminant `Δ₂(n)`, built from `p, q, r`, whose eventual sign
governs log-convexity, reducing to `γβ − αδ` when `r ≡ 0`.

**The key insight is** that the log-behaviour of a P-recursive sequence should be
readable from a single discriminant polynomial of its recurrence coefficients,
exactly as the quadratic discriminant reads off the sign of a quadratic form.

**Why now?** The first-order case is now fully understood as the `r ≡ 0`
specialization; the Motzkin and Baxter numbers give concrete second-order test
cases with known log-convexity, providing immediate falsification targets.

## Conjecture C — Renormalized totals and infinite log-concavity

Dividing a strictly log-convex total by its exact growth ratio
`(γ n + δ)/(α n + β)` yields a renormalized sequence whose discriminant is
identically zero (log-linear); we conjecture that a *second* renormalization by
the discriminant of the ratio itself produces a strictly log-concave residual,
and that iterating this process terminates in a sequence that is infinitely
log-concave.

**The key insight is** that the Möbius ratio is precisely the correction factor
needed to flatten log-curvature, so peeling it off should expose successively
higher-order convexity data in a controlled tower.

**Why now?** The exact growth ratio is now available in closed form for every
classical total, so the first renormalization step can be carried out
explicitly and its residual tested for the next-order sign.

## Conjecture D — Tropical/valuation dequantization of the trichotomy

Writing `v(n) = −log a(n)`, the trichotomy becomes a statement about the second
difference `Δ²v(n) = v(n) − 2v(n+1) + v(n+2)`: strictly negative, zero, or
strictly positive according to `sign(Δ)`. We conjecture that for the recurrence
class this second difference is *monotone in `n`* and converges to `0`, so the
valuation is asymptotically affine with a computable curvature defect controlled
by `Δ`.

**The key insight is** that log-convexity is exactly convexity of the valuation,
so the discriminant `Δ` should appear as the leading coefficient of the
piecewise-linear (tropical) profile of the sequence.

**Why now?** The equivalence between strict log-convexity and strict convexity
of the logarithm is already in hand; casting it in valuation form turns the
trichotomy into a discrete-convexity statement amenable to summation-by-parts
estimates.

This cycle formalizes, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, the *combinatorial core* of the

/-!
# The Alexandrov Topology of the Forcing Multiverse

**Direction 4 of the research programme — a topology/modal-logic bridge.**

The combinatorial core of the forcing multiverse (`ModalFrame.lean`) equips the
class of worlds `W` with an accessibility relation `R` (read *"is a forcing
extension of"*) and two operators on assertions `P : W → Prop`:

* `box R P w`  — `P` holds in *every* forcing extension of `w` (necessity);
* `dia R P w`  — `P` holds in *some* forcing extension of `w` (possibility).

Here we show these modal operators are **not merely formal**: when `R` is a
preorder (reflexive + transitive — validating axioms **T** and **4**), the
assertions carry a genuine *topology*, the **Alexandrov topology** whose open sets
are the `R`-upward-closed sets, and under this topology

* `box`  *is* the topological **interior** operator (`interior_eq_box`);
* `dia`  *is* the topological **closure** operator (`closure_eq_dia`).

Consequently the buttons of Direction 2 (the `box`-fixed assertions) are exactly
the **open** sets (`isOpen_iff_box_fixed`), and the *settled* assertions — those
whose truth value is invariant along forcing — are exactly the **clopen** sets
(`isClopen_iff_invariant`).  The space is moreover **Alexandrov-discrete**
(`alexandrov_discrete`): arbitrary intersections of opens are open, the
distinguishing feature separating these preorder-topologies from ordinary ones.

Finally we connect back to the quantitative picture of Direction 5: in the
*fully connected* multiverse (`R = ⊤`, every world a forcing extension of every
other — the `S5` situation) the only clopen assertions are the two constants
`⊥` and `⊤` (`isClopen_complete_iff`).  This is the topological face of
`card_settled = 2`: **the settled assertions are exactly the two truth-constants,
everything else is genuinely independent.**

Everything is proved from first principles over `Mathlib`, reusing the `box`/`dia`
definitions of the catalog's `ModalFrame` core.

namespace Multiverse

open Multiverse

variable {W : Type*} (R : W → W → Prop)

/-! ## Upper sets and the Alexandrov topology -/

/-- An assertion `S` is an **upper set** (upward closed) for `R` when it is
preserved along accessibility: if `w ∈ S` and `w` accesses `v`, then `v ∈ S`.
These are the "forcing-stable" assertions: once true they stay true in every
extension. -/
def IsUpSet (S : Set W) : Prop := ∀ ⦃w v⦄, R w v → w ∈ S → v ∈ S

/-- The **Alexandrov topology** of the accessibility relation `R`: the open sets
are exactly the `R`-upper sets.  This is a topology for *any* relation `R`
whatsoever — no frame conditions are needed to define it. -/
def alexandrovForcing : TopologicalSpace W where
  IsOpen S := IsUpSet R S
  isOpen_univ := by intro w v _ _; trivial
  isOpen_inter := by
    intro S T hS hT w v hwv hw; exact ⟨hS hwv hw.1, hT hwv hw.2⟩
  isOpen_sUnion := by
    intro F hF w v hwv hw
    obtain ⟨s, hsF, hws⟩ := hw
    exact ⟨s, hsF, hF s hsF hwv hws⟩

/-- By definition, the open sets of the Alexandrov topology are the upper sets. -/
theorem isOpen_alexandrovForcing_iff (S : Set W) :
    @IsOpen W (alexandrovForcing R) S ↔ IsUpSet R S := Iff.rfl

/-! ## The Sahlqvist correspondence, topologically: `box` = interior, `dia` = closure -/

/-- **`box` is the interior operator.**  Over a preorder (reflexive + transitive
`R` — i.e. validating axioms **T** and **4**), the necessity operator `box`
computes exactly the topological interior in the Alexandrov topology: the largest
forcing-stable assertion implying `S`. -/
theorem interior_eq_box (hR : Reflexive R) (hT : Transitive R) (S : Set W) :
    @interior W (alexandrovForcing R) S = {w | box R (· ∈ S) w} := by
  letI : TopologicalSpace W := alexandrovForcing R
  apply le_antisymm
  · intro w hw v hwv
    have hos : IsOpen (interior S) := isOpen_interior
    exact interior_subset (hos hwv hw)
  · intro w hw
    have hopen : IsOpen {w | box R (· ∈ S) w} := by
      intro a b hab ha c hbc; exact ha c (hT hab hbc)
    have hsub : {w | box R (· ∈ S) w} ⊆ S := fun a ha => ha a (hR a)
    exact interior_maximal hsub hopen hw

operator `dia` computes exactly the topological closure: the smallest
forcing-costable assertion implied by `S`. -/
theorem closure_eq_dia (hR : Reflexive R) (hT : Transitive R) (S : Set W) :
    @closure W (alexandrovForcing R) S = {w | dia R (· ∈ S) w} := by
  letI : TopologicalSpace W := alexandrovForcing R

the interior of a preorder-topology is idempotent. -/
theorem box_box_eq_box (hR : Reflexive R) (hT : Transitive R) (S : Set W) :

  letI : TopologicalSpace W := alexandrovForcing R
  have h1 := interior_eq_box R hR hT S
  have h2 := interior_eq_box R hR hT {w | box R (· ∈ S) w}

  · intro h a b hab ha
    exact (h a).1 ha b hab

import Mathlib

/-!
# The Modal Logic of the Forcing Multiverse: Frame Correspondences

This file develops the abstract Kripke-frame core behind the *modal logic of
forcing* in the set-theoretic multiverse.  A "world" is a model of set theory and
the accessibility relation `R` is read as *"is a forcing extension of"*.

For a relation `R : W → W → Prop` we define the box (necessity: *true in every
accessible extension*) and diamond (possibility: *true in some accessible
extension*) operators on assertions `P : W → Prop`, and prove the classical
*Sahlqvist frame correspondences* linking the modal axioms to first-order frame
conditions:

* `box_toPoint_iff_reflexive`   —  axiom **T** `□p → p`     ↔ reflexivity;
* `box_box_iff_transitive`      —  axiom **4** `□p → □□p`   ↔ transitivity;
* `brouwer_iff_symmetric`       —  axiom **B** `p → □◇p`    ↔ symmetry;
* `euclid_iff_euclidean`        —  axiom **5** `◇p → □◇p`   ↔ euclideanness;
* `directed_iff_confluent`      —  axiom **.2** `◇□p → □◇p` ↔ confluence (directedness).

The upshot (`nat_le_frame_is_S42_not_S5`) is the content of Direction 1 of the
research programme: the *directed but antisymmetric* forcing-extension order —
modelled by `(ℕ, ≤)` — validates **T**, **4** and **.2** but refutes **B** and
**5**.  Symmetry is exactly the frame condition whose loss drops `S5` to the
Hamkins–Löwe logic `S4.2`.
-/

namespace Multiverse

variable {W : Type*} (R : W → W → Prop)

/-- Necessity: `p` holds in every world accessible from `w`. -/
def box (P : W → Prop) (w : W) : Prop := ∀ v, R w v → P v

/-- Possibility: `p` holds in some world accessible from `w`. -/
def dia (P : W → Prop) (w : W) : Prop := ∃ v, R w v ∧ P v

/-- A relation is **euclidean** when any two worlds accessible from a common world
are mutually accessible in one direction (`R x y → R x z → R y z`). -/
def Euclidean : Prop := ∀ ⦃x y z⦄, R x y → R x z → R y z

/-- A relation is **confluent** / **directed** when any two worlds accessible from
a common world have a common accessible successor.  This is the "directedness" of
iterated forcing: two extensions can be amalgamated. -/
def Confluent : Prop := ∀ ⦃x y z⦄, R x y → R x z → ∃ u, R y u ∧ R z u

/-! ## Frame correspondences -/

/-
**Axiom T** `□p → p` is valid on the frame iff `R` is reflexive.
-/
theorem box_toPoint_iff_reflexive :
    (∀ (P : W → Prop) w, box R P w → P w) ↔ Reflexive R := by
  constructor;
  · exact fun h x => h _ x fun _ h' => h';
  · intro hR P w hP; exact hP w (hR w)

/-
**Axiom 4** `□p → □□p` is valid on the frame iff `R` is transitive.
-/
theorem box_box_iff_transitive :
    (∀ (P : W → Prop) w, box R P w → box R (box R P) w) ↔ Transitive R := by
  refine' ⟨ _, fun h P w hw x hx => _ ⟩;
  · intro h x y z hxy hyz;
    specialize h ( fun v => R x v ) x ; simp_all +decide [ box ];
    exact h _ hxy _ hyz;
  · exact fun y hy => hw y ( h hx hy )

/-
**Axiom B** `p → □◇p` (Brouwer) is valid on the frame iff `R` is symmetric.
-/
theorem brouwer_iff_symmetric :
    (∀ (P : W → Prop) w, P w → box R (dia R P) w) ↔ Symmetric R := by
  refine' ⟨ fun h => _, fun h => _ ⟩;
  · intro x y hxy; specialize h ( fun z => z = x ) x; simp_all +decide [ box, dia ] ;
  · intro P w hw v hv
    use w;
    exact ⟨ h hv, hw ⟩

/-
**Axiom 5** `◇p → □◇p` is valid on the frame iff `R` is euclidean.
-/
theorem euclid_iff_euclidean :
    (∀ (P : W → Prop) w, dia R P w → box R (dia R P) w) ↔ Euclidean R := by
  constructor <;> intro h;
  · intro x y z hxy hxz; specialize h ( fun w => w = z ) x; simp_all +decide [ box, dia ] ;
  · exact fun P w ⟨ v, hv, hv' ⟩ x hx => ⟨ v, h hx hv, hv' ⟩

/-
**Axiom .2** `◇□p → □◇p` (directedness) is valid on the frame iff `R` is
confluent.  This is the axiom separating `S4.2` from `S4`.
-/
theorem directed_iff_confluent :
    (∀ (P : W → Prop) w, dia R (box R P) w → box R (dia R P) w) ↔ Confluent R := by
  constructor;
  · intro h x y z hxy hxz;
    specialize h ( fun w => R z w ) x;
    grind +locals;
  · intros h P w hw; intro v hv; obtain ⟨ a, ha₁, ha₂ ⟩ := hw; obtain ⟨ u, hu₁, hu₂ ⟩ := h hv ha₁; use u; aesop;

/-! ## The forcing-extension order `(ℕ, ≤)` is genuinely `S4.2`, not `S5` -/

/-
The extension order is reflexive.
-/
theorem nat_le_reflexive : Reflexive (· ≤ · : ℕ → ℕ → Prop) := by
  exact fun x => le_refl x

/-
The extension order is transitive.
-/
theorem nat_le_transitive : Transitive (· ≤ · : ℕ → ℕ → Prop) := by
  exact fun x y z hxy hyz => le_trans hxy hyz

/-
The extension order is confluent/directed: any two extensions amalgamate.
-/
theorem nat_le_confluent : Confluent (· ≤ · : ℕ → ℕ → Prop) := by
  exact fun x y z h1 h2 => ⟨ Max.max y z, le_max_left _ _, le_max_right _ _ ⟩

/-
The extension order is **not** symmetric.
-/
theorem nat_le_not_symmetric : ¬ Symmetric (· ≤ · : ℕ → ℕ → Prop) := by
  exact fun h => by have := @h 0 1; norm_num at this;

/-
The extension order is **not** euclidean.
-/
theorem nat_le_not_euclidean : ¬ Euclidean (· ≤ · : ℕ → ℕ → Prop) := by
  exact fun h => by have := @h 0 1 0; norm_num at this;

/-
**Direction 1, main separation.**  On the directed antisymmetric forcing
order `(ℕ, ≤)`, the modal axioms **T**, **4** and **.2** are valid, while **B**
and **5** both fail.  Hence the logic of directed forcing is `S4.2`, strictly
weaker than the `S5` obtained from a symmetric (equivalence) accessibility.
-/
theorem nat_le_frame_is_S42_not_S5 :
    -- T holds
    (∀ (P : ℕ → Prop) w, box (· ≤ ·) P w → P w) ∧
    -- 4 holds
    (∀ (P : ℕ → Prop) w, box (· ≤ ·) P w → box (· ≤ ·) (box (· ≤ ·) P) w) ∧
    -- .2 holds
    (∀ (P : ℕ → Prop) w, dia (· ≤ ·) (box (· ≤ ·) P) w → box (· ≤ ·) (dia (· ≤ ·) P) w) ∧
    -- B fails
    (¬ ∀ (P : ℕ → Prop) w, P w → box (· ≤ ·) (dia (· ≤ ·) P) w) ∧
    -- 5 fails
    (¬ ∀ (P : ℕ → Prop) w, dia (· ≤ ·) P w → box (· ≤ ·) (dia (· ≤ ·) P) w) := by
  grind +suggestions

end Multiverse

equivalence of categories between forcing frames and Alexandrov spaces.

# Future Directions — Spectral gaps of fixed-genus chord-swap chains

This cycle established, unconditionally, that the variational (Rayleigh-quotient)
upper bound for a one-dimensional swap chain scales as `Θ(n^{-3})`: a monotone
statistic that changes by one unit per move has Dirichlet energy of order `n`
and variance of order `n⁴`, and the ratio pins the gap upper bound to the cubic
window `[6 n^{-3}, 12 n^{-3}]`.  The conjectures below extend this mechanism from
the model path chain to the genuine fixed-genus chord-swap chain and beyond.

## Conjecture 1 — Cubic upper bound for the fixed-genus chord-swap gap

For every fixed genus `g`, the spectral gap of the chord-swap chain on chord
diagrams with `n` chords satisfies `γ_{n,g} = O(n^{-3})`.

The key insight is that thickening a chord diagram produces a monotone
genus-aware "spread" statistic — for instance the total nesting-plus-crossing
index — that a single swap changes by a bounded amount, so its Dirichlet energy
grows linearly in `n` while its variance grows quartically; the quotient is
exactly the cubic order isolated for the path model.

Why now? The energy/variance bookkeeping that forces the exponent has now been
carried out in full for the one-dimensional prototype, reducing the chord-swap
upper bound to the concrete combinatorial task of exhibiting one monotone,
unit-step, quartic-variance statistic on the diagram space.

## Conjecture 2 — Matching cubic lower bound (tightness of the exponent)

For every fixed genus `g`, the spectral gap obeys `γ_{n,g} = Ω(n^{-3})`, so that
combined with Conjecture 1 the exponent is exactly three: `γ_{n,g} = Θ(n^{-3})`.

The key insight is that a canonical-path (multicommodity-flow) routing of unit
mass between diagrams, in which each swap edge carries flow proportional to the
length of the paths through it, incurs congestion of order `n³`; the standard
duality between congestion and the Poincaré constant then converts the `O(n³)`
relaxation time into the matching `Ω(n^{-3})` gap.

Why now? The upper bound identifies `n³` as the intrinsic time scale, which tells
the lower-bound designer exactly the congestion budget a good routing must meet,
turning an open exponent question into a calibrated flow-construction problem.

## Conjecture 3 — Genus enters only through the constant, not the exponent

Write `γ_{n,g} = c(g) · n^{-3} (1 + o(1))` as `n → ∞`.  Then the leading constant
`c(g)` is a strictly decreasing, strictly positive function of the genus `g`, and
the exponent `-3` is independent of `g`.

The key insight is that fixing the genus caps the number of topologically
distinct local obstructions a swap must resolve, so genus rescales the effective
conductance (hence the constant) without altering the one-dimensional diffusive
geometry that produces the cubic exponent.

Why now? With the exponent understood, the residual `g`-dependence is isolated in
a single measurable amplitude `c(g)`, which can be estimated from moderate-size
diagrams and compared across genera to test monotonicity directly.

## Conjecture 4 — Universality across unit-step swap statistics

Any reversible swap chain on a combinatorial family that carries a monotone
integer statistic changing by `±1` per move, and whose stationary law spreads
that statistic across a range of order `n` with variance of order `n⁴`, has
spectral gap of order `n^{-3}`.

The key insight is that the cubic exponent is a property of the statistic's
energy-to-variance ratio, not of the specific objects being shuffled, so perfect
matchings, chord diagrams, and lattice paths should all share the same exponent
whenever their driving statistic has the linear-energy / quartic-variance
profile.

Why now? The prototype computation shows the exponent depends only on these two
growth rates, making the universality statement a precise, falsifiable prediction
that can be checked family by family.
